column1: # Curated packet annotations - the human-meaningful layer on top of the
#   direction: S = client->server only, R = server->client only, B = both
#   short-name: the label shown in the overlay / logger
#   description: one line, what the packet means
#   - the recovered id->class map (Ghidra: CNetMsg::CreateNetMsg, FUN_00f41fce)
# Anything not listed here still gets its class name from ids_recv.tsv; this
# table only overrides / enriches the entries that actually matter in a session.
# ---- login / handshake (login server: 0x04xx..0x09xx before world entry) ----

column4: Login step 1: server sends the encryption seed ("CMsgEncryptCode"). Seeds the client's 16-byte key table. 8 bytes.
Login step 2: client answers with the account/auth blob ("CMsgAccountEx", 472 B). Built from res.dat + machine key; body is opaque (encrypted credentials), not protobuf.
Login step 4: 324-byte session challenge ("CMsgConnectEx") - repeated key blocks + 32-char hex session hash. Server list + key material.
Login step 5: client's 52-byte reply to the session challenge.
Machine/hardware fingerprint upload (188 B), ~14 s after login. 6 raw bytes hex-encoded; anti-cheat client attestation.
Compact server info / ack after world entry.
Heartbeat / item-ping tick (12 B each way). The steady keep-alive.
Movement sync. SEND = client walk request (target pos); RECV = authoritative position broadcast.
Entity action (attack / cast / interact animation). Body is CMsgAction; the real sub-type is a field inside the protobuf (e.g. actionGetItemSet).
Interact with npc/object (attack, gather, dialogue trigger).
Player/entity spawn + periodic full stat snapshot (id, hp, mp, pos, name...). The dense one, ~288 per session.
Chat + system message feed. Bodies carry the text.
Chat line (CMsgTalk). Carries speaker, channel, message.
Mailbox list (sender/subject encoded in the body).
Ground-item / map-item move sync (CMsgMapItem). ~198 per side.
Npc/player drop event (CMsgNpcInfo context), 62 per session.
Attribute list for an entity (per-entity stat rows).
